gloss: original language; original word; source language

definitions.explanation: The language in which a text was originally written or spoken, as contrasted with a translation. Also refers to a word in its source language before being translated or borrowed.

examples.japanese: {原語|げんご}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{読|よ}んで→読む：00426_yomu⟧みたい。
examples.english: I'd like to read it in the original language.

examples.japanese: ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{言葉|ことば}→言葉：02880_kotoba⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{原語|げんご}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧ラテン⟦{語|ご}→〜語：09841_go⟧だ。
examples.english: The original of this word is Latin.

examples.japanese: {原語|げんご}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦ニュアンス→ニュアンス：11138_nyuansu⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{翻訳|ほんやく}→翻訳：01725_honyaku⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{完全|かんぜん}→完全：01552_kanzen⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{伝|つた}わらない→伝わる：01961_tsutawaru⟧。
examples.english: The nuance of the original language cannot be fully conveyed in translation.

notes:
Composed of {原|げん} (origin) + ⟦{語|ご}→〜語：09841_go⟧ (language, word). Note the homophone ⟦{言語|げんご}→言語：02717_gengo⟧ (language in the general sense) — context usually makes the distinction clear.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {原語|げんご}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{読|よ}む→読む：00426_yomu⟧: to read in the original
- {原語|げんご}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{意味|いみ}→意味：01155_imi⟧: the meaning in the source language
- {原語|げんご}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{忠実|ちゅうじつ}→忠実：12570_chuujitsu⟧な⟦{翻訳|ほんやく}→翻訳：01725_honyaku⟧: a translation faithful to the original

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{原文|げんぶん}→原文：20563_genbun⟧: the original text — refers to the actual passage of text rather than the language itself
- {訳語|やくご}: translated word — the counterpart concept, i.e., the word chosen in the target language
